To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetic field of the MURA accelerator was measured and corrected.
the magnetic fields in a 50‐Mev electron accelerator can be measured with an accuracy of about 2 G and can be corrected to a precision of about 1 G.
we were able to correct the field errors in the MURA electron accelerator to within 2.5% of the design values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of the accelerator system and with methods for measuring and correcting the magnetic fields in the accelerator.
the measurement of the magnetic fields, the correction of these fields, the design of the accelerator and its associated equipment, and the operation of the accelerator.
the development of a method of measuring the magnetic field of an accelerator, and the correction of errors in that field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MURA 200‐kG magnet system is a very good magnet system.
the magnetic fields of MURA were measured, corrected, and controlled to the required tolerances and that the magnetic field quality of the accelerator was excellent.
the MURA 5‐MeV electron machine has been corrected to the required accuracy, that the corrections are stable and repeatable, and that the machine is now operating at the design current.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic fields were measured and corrected to within the required accuracy.
the MURA 2000‐MeV electron machine, which was built using the same magnet technology, has a field quality which is within the tolerances required for its design.
we have achieved the required field quality with a minimum of effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field quality can be significantly improved by the application of computer methods to the design, construction and alignment of the magnets.
the use of computer methods to design and evaluate the corrections is a very powerful tool.
it is possible to achieve good magnetic field uniformity over the entire beam cross section of a high‐current accelerator.
